āpa: [Āpa]  CL=1 (1) Water in rivers, creeks, brooks, ponds, etc., which arises along with vaṇṇa (beauty) and gandha (fragrance), is called sasambhāra-āpa (water with composite properties). (2) The āpodhātu represents the characteristic of fluidity, moistness, or the essence of liquidity. (See also āpodhātu for further details.) (3) Water that serves as the paṭibhāganimitta (counterpart sign) for meditation practice is referred to as āpa kasiṇa. It is also called ārammaṇā āpa (water as an object of meditation) or nimitta āpa (water as a meditation sign). See also - āpokasiṇa. (4) A deva named Āpa: After meditating on the āpa kasiṇa, one who attains āpa kasiṇa jhāna and, upon passing away, is reborn in the deva realm. Such beings are named Āpa by their previous meditative attainments. This is also called sammuti āpa (a conventional designation based on past deeds). (5) Locations characterized by water, such as oceans, are called āpa. See – āpagā.
